facts.text: Houston Siding, the town’s original name, first appeared on an Alaska Railroad blueprint in 1917 and was named after Congressman Houston of Tennessee.
The Little Susitna River cuts through Houston, carving a floodplain that shapes local hydrology with gravel bars and riparian zones.
Recent studies warn of rising wildfire risk in Houston, driven by spruce bark beetles that kill trees and extend fire seasons.
Houston experiences extreme daylight swings, with winter days as short as 5 hours 18 minutes and summer days exceeding 19 hours.
Houston is the only place in Southcentral Alaska where fireworks can be legally purchased, a policy that helps fund emergency services.
